goal.objective:
Finish `src/heap.js` and `src/dijkstra.js`. `IndexedHeap` is a binary min-heap that also keeps an index from key to position, so `push`, `pop`, `remove`, `decreaseKey`, and `setPriority` each run in O(log n) while `has`, `peek`, and `priorityOf` are O(1). The starting point scans a plain array and leaves the keyed operations unimplemented; replace it with the real structure.

Every entry has a string key that is unique within the heap and a finite numeric priority; smaller priorities leave first, and negative and fractional priorities are ordinary. Entries with equal priority leave in the order they were pushed. Each entry is stamped with an insertion number when it is pushed, and that number never changes afterwards, so an entry whose priority is raised and then lowered back still leaves before entries pushed after it. `push(key, priority)` adds an entry; `peek()` returns `{ key, priority }` for the next entry without removing it, and `pop()` removes and returns it; both return `undefined` on an empty heap. `has(key)` and `priorityOf(key)` report what is held. `decreaseKey(key, priority)` lowers a priority, accepting an unchanged one. `setPriority(key, priority)` moves a priority in either direction. `remove(key)` drops any held key and returns whether it did. `drain()` empties the heap and returns every entry in pop order. `size` reports how many entries are held.

`src/dijkstra.js` exports `shortestPaths(graph, source)` and `shortestPath(graph, source, target)` over a weighted directed graph — a plain object mapping each node id to an object of successor ids and weights, each weight a finite number greater than zero. Drive the search with the heap: when a shorter route to a node that is already queued turns up, lower that node's priority in place rather than queueing the node twice. `shortestPaths` returns `{ dist, prev }` covering every node of the graph, with `Infinity` and `null` for a node the source cannot reach. Where several shortest routes to a node tie, `prev` names the smallest predecessor id among them, so the answer never depends on the order nodes came off the queue. `shortestPath` returns `{ distance, path }` with `path` running from source to target, or `null` when the target is unreachable.

Errors are specific. A heap key that is not a string raises `TypeError` with message `key must be a string`; a priority that is not a finite number raises `TypeError` with message `priority must be a finite number`; pushing a key that is already held raises `Error` with message `duplicate key: "a"`; re-prioritising a key that is not held raises `ReferenceError` with message `unknown key: "a"`; and a `decreaseKey` that would raise a priority raises `RangeError` with message `priority must not increase for "a"`. A graph that is not a non-null, non-array object raises `TypeError` with message `graph must be an object`; a node whose successors are not such an object raises `TypeError` with message `edge map for node "a" must be an object`; an edge or endpoint naming an undeclared node raises `ReferenceError` with message `unknown node: "q"`; a weight that is not a positive finite number raises `RangeError` with message `weight must be positive: "a" -> "b"`; and a non-string source raises `TypeError` with message `source must be a string`. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.

Track every background job id you start. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

1: import { test } from 'node:test';
2: import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
3: 
4: import { IndexedHeap } from '../src/heap.js';
5: 
6: /**
7:  * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG.
8:  * @param {number} seed Initial state.
9:  * @returns {() => number} Generator returning floats in [0, 1).
10:  */
11: function mulberry32(seed) {
12:   let a = seed >>> 0;
13:   return () => {
14:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
15:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
16:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
17:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
18:   };
19: }
20: 
21: test('an empty heap reports nothing', () => {
22:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
23:   assert.deepEqual([heap.size, heap.peek(), heap.pop(), heap.drain()], [0, undefined, undefined, []]);
24:   assert.deepEqual([heap.has('nope'), heap.priorityOf('nope'), heap.remove('nope')], [false, undefined, false]);
25: });
26: 
27: test('entries leave in priority order', () => {
28:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
29:   for (const [key, priority] of [['e', 5], ['a', 1], ['d', 4], ['c', 3], ['b', 2]]) heap.push(key, priority);
30:   assert.equal(heap.size, 5);
31:   assert.deepEqual(heap.peek(), { key: 'a', priority: 1 });
32:   assert.deepEqual(heap.pop(), { key: 'a', priority: 1 });
33:   assert.deepEqual(heap.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['b', 'c', 'd', 'e']);
34:   assert.equal(heap.size, 0);
35:   const negatives = new IndexedHeap();
36:   for (const [key, priority] of [['zero', 0], ['neg', -3.5], ['pos', 0.5]]) negatives.push(key, priority);
37:   assert.deepEqual(negatives.drain(), [
38:     { key: 'neg', priority: -3.5 },
39:     { key: 'zero', priority: 0 },
40:     { key: 'pos', priority: 0.5 },
41:   ]);
42: });
43: 
44: test('equal priorities leave in insertion order', () => {
45:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
46:   for (const key of ['p', 'q', 'r', 's', 't', 'u', 'v']) heap.push(key, 5);
47:   assert.deepEqual(heap.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['p', 'q', 'r', 's', 't', 'u', 'v']);
48:   const mixed = new IndexedHeap();
49:   for (const [key, priority] of [['a', 2], ['b', 1], ['c', 2], ['d', 1], ['e', 2]]) mixed.push(key, priority);
50:   assert.deepEqual(mixed.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['b', 'd', 'a', 'c', 'e']);
51: });
52: 
53: test('re-prioritising keeps the original insertion number', () => {
54:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
55:   for (const key of ['x', 'y', 'z']) heap.push(key, 1);
56:   heap.setPriority('x', 9);
57:   assert.deepEqual(heap.peek(), { key: 'y', priority: 1 });
58:   heap.setPriority('x', 1);
59:   assert.deepEqual(heap.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['x', 'y', 'z']);
60:   const again = new IndexedHeap();
61:   for (const key of ['x', 'y', 'z']) again.push(key, 1);
62:   again.decreaseKey('z', 1);
63:   assert.deepEqual(again.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['x', 'y', 'z']);
64: });
65: 
66: test('decreaseKey lowers a priority and refuses to raise one', () => {
67:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
68:   for (const [key, priority] of [['a', 10], ['b', 20], ['c', 30], ['d', 40]]) heap.push(key, priority);
69:   heap.decreaseKey('d', 5);
70:   assert.deepEqual(heap.peek(), { key: 'd', priority: 5 });
71:   assert.equal(heap.priorityOf('d'), 5);
72:   assert.throws(() => heap.decreaseKey('d', 6), { name: 'RangeError', message: 'priority must not increase for "d"' });
73:   assert.throws(() => heap.decreaseKey('gone', 1), { name: 'ReferenceError', message: 'unknown key: "gone"' });
74:   assert.throws(() => heap.setPriority('gone', 1), { name: 'ReferenceError', message: 'unknown key: "gone"' });
75:   heap.setPriority('a', 99);
76:   assert.deepEqual(heap.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['d', 'b', 'c', 'a']);
77: });
78: 
79: test('remove takes an entry from anywhere and keeps the order intact', () => {
80:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
81:   for (const [key, priority] of [['a', 1], ['b', 2], ['c', 3], ['d', 4], ['e', 5], ['f', 6], ['g', 7]]) {
82:     heap.push(key, priority);
83:   }
84:   assert.equal(heap.remove('a'), true);
85:   assert.equal(heap.remove('g'), true);
86:   assert.equal(heap.remove('d'), true);
87:   assert.equal(heap.remove('d'), false);
88:   assert.deepEqual([heap.size, heap.has('d'), heap.priorityOf('c')], [4, false, 3]);
89:   assert.deepEqual(heap.drain().map((entry) => entry.key), ['b', 'c', 'e', 'f']);
90:   const single = new IndexedHeap();
91:   single.push('only', 1);
92:   assert.equal(single.remove('only'), true);
93:   assert.deepEqual([single.size, single.peek()], [0, undefined]);
94: });

96: test('rejects malformed keys and priorities', () => {
97:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
98:   heap.push('a', 1);
99:   const bad = [
100:     [() => heap.push('a', 2), 'Error', 'duplicate key: "a"'],
101:     [() => heap.push(1, 1), 'TypeError', 'key must be a string'],
102:     [() => heap.has(null), 'TypeError', 'key must be a string'],
103:     [() => heap.push('b', Number.NaN), 'TypeError', 'priority must be a finite number'],
104:     [() => heap.push('b', Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY), 'TypeError', 'priority must be a finite number'],
105:     [() => heap.push('b', '5'), 'TypeError', 'priority must be a finite number'],
106:     [() => heap.decreaseKey('a', Number.NaN), 'TypeError', 'priority must be a finite number'],
107:   ];
108:   for (const [call, name, message] of bad) assert.throws(call, { name, message }, message);
109:   assert.deepEqual([heap.size, heap.has('b')], [1, false]);
110: });

112: test('matches a naive model across a long random operation sequence', () => {
113:   const rnd = mulberry32(0x1e4d);
114:   const keyPool = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => `k${String(i).padStart(2, '0')}`);
115:   const heap = new IndexedHeap();
116:   /** @type {Array<{key: string, priority: number, seq: number}>} */
117:   let model = [];
118:   let seq = 0;
119:   const best = () => {
120:     let winner = null;
121:     for (const item of model) {
122:       if (winner === null || item.priority < winner.priority || (item.priority === winner.priority && item.seq < winner.seq)) {
123:         winner = item;
124:       }
125:     }
126:     return winner;
127:   };
128: 
129:   for (let step = 0; step < 6000; step += 1) {
130:     const key = keyPool[Math.floor(rnd() * keyPool.length)];
131:     const held = model.find((item) => item.key === key);
132:     const roll = rnd();
133:     if (roll < 0.4) {
134:       const priority = Math.floor(rnd() * 8);
135:       if (held === undefined) {
136:         heap.push(key, priority);
137:         seq += 1;
138:         model.push({ key, priority, seq });
139:       } else {
140:         assert.throws(() => heap.push(key, priority), { name: 'Error', message: `duplicate key: "${key}"` }, `step ${step}`);
141:       }
142:     } else if (roll < 0.65) {
143:       const winner = best();
144:       const popped = heap.pop();
145:       if (winner === null) assert.equal(popped, undefined, `step ${step}`);
146:       else {
147:         assert.deepEqual(popped, { key: winner.key, priority: winner.priority }, `pop at step ${step}`);
148:         model = model.filter((item) => item !== winner);
149:       }
150:     } else if (roll < 0.8 && held !== undefined) {
151:       const priority = held.priority - Math.floor(rnd() * 4);
152:       heap.decreaseKey(key, priority);
153:       held.priority = priority;
154:     } else if (roll < 0.9 && held !== undefined) {
155:       const priority = Math.floor(rnd() * 12) - 2;
156:       heap.setPriority(key, priority);
157:       held.priority = priority;
158:     } else {
159:       assert.equal(heap.remove(key), held !== undefined, `remove at step ${step}`);
160:       model = model.filter((item) => item !== held);
161:     }
162:     assert.deepEqual([heap.size, heap.priorityOf(key)], [model.length, model.find((i) => i.key === key)?.priority], `state at step ${step}`);
163:   }
164: 
165:   const drained = heap.drain();
166:   const expected = [...model].sort((a, b) => a.priority - b.priority || a.seq - b.seq);
167:   assert.deepEqual(drained, expected.map(({ key, priority }) => ({ key, priority })));
168:   assert.deepEqual([heap.size, heap.pop()], [0, undefined]);
169: });

**`src/heap.js`** — a real binary min-heap backed by an array plus a `Map` from key to position:
- Entries carry `{key, priority, seq}`; `seq` is stamped once at push and never changes, so equal priorities leave in insertion order even after a re-prioritisation round trip.
- `#siftUp`/`#siftDown` update the index on every move, giving O(log n) `push`, `pop`, `remove`, `decreaseKey`, `setPriority` and O(1) `has`, `peek`, `priorityOf`.

**`src/dijkstra.js`** — heap-driven search:
- Validates the graph (object shape, edge maps, undeclared endpoints, positive finite weights) and the source/target before searching.

- Predecessors are chosen in a separate pass over nodes in sorted id order, picking the smallest predecessor that realises each node's distance — so `prev` is independent of pop order and ties resolve deterministically.
- `shortestPath` walks `prev` back from the target, returning `null` when unreachable.

goal.objective:
Finish `src/heap.js` and `src/dijkstra.js`. `IndexedHeap` is a binary min-heap that also keeps an index from key to position, so `push`, `pop`, `remove`, `decreaseKey`, and `setPriority` each run in O(log n) while `has`, `peek`, and `priorityOf` are O(1). The starting point scans a plain array and leaves the keyed operations unimplemented; replace it with the real structure.

Every entry has a string key that is unique within the heap and a finite numeric priority; smaller priorities leave first, and negative and fractional priorities are ordinary. Entries with equal priority leave in the order they were pushed. Each entry is stamped with an insertion number when it is pushed, and that number never changes afterwards, so an entry whose priority is raised and then lowered back still leaves before entries pushed after it. `push(key, priority)` adds an entry; `peek()` returns `{ key, priority }` for the next entry without removing it, and `pop()` removes and returns it; both return `undefined` on an empty heap. `has(key)` and `priorityOf(key)` report what is held. `decreaseKey(key, priority)` lowers a priority, accepting an unchanged one. `setPriority(key, priority)` moves a priority in either direction. `remove(key)` drops any held key and returns whether it did. `drain()` empties the heap and returns every entry in pop order. `size` reports how many entries are held.

`src/dijkstra.js` exports `shortestPaths(graph, source)` and `shortestPath(graph, source, target)` over a weighted directed graph — a plain object mapping each node id to an object of successor ids and weights, each weight a finite number greater than zero. Drive the search with the heap: when a shorter route to a node that is already queued turns up, lower that node's priority in place rather than queueing the node twice. `shortestPaths` returns `{ dist, prev }` covering every node of the graph, with `Infinity` and `null` for a node the source cannot reach. Where several shortest routes to a node tie, `prev` names the smallest predecessor id among them, so the answer never depends on the order nodes came off the queue. `shortestPath` returns `{ distance, path }` with `path` running from source to target, or `null` when the target is unreachable.

Errors are specific. A heap key that is not a string raises `TypeError` with message `key must be a string`; a priority that is not a finite number raises `TypeError` with message `priority must be a finite number`; pushing a key that is already held raises `Error` with message `duplicate key: "a"`; re-prioritising a key that is not held raises `ReferenceError` with message `unknown key: "a"`; and a `decreaseKey` that would raise a priority raises `RangeError` with message `priority must not increase for "a"`. A graph that is not a non-null, non-array object raises `TypeError` with message `graph must be an object`; a node whose successors are not such an object raises `TypeError` with message `edge map for node "a" must be an object`; an edge or endpoint naming an undeclared node raises `ReferenceError` with message `unknown node: "q"`; a weight that is not a positive finite number raises `RangeError` with message `weight must be positive: "a" -> "b"`; and a non-string source raises `TypeError` with message `source must be a string`.
